question.text: Let <math><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo><</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math> be positive integers such that <math><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math> . Then the number of such distinct arrangements <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> is _________

solution.text:
When n5 takes value from 10 to 6 the carry forward moves from 0 to 4 which can be arranged in 4C0+4C14+4C22+4C41=7
Alternate solution
Possible solutions are
1, 2, 3, 4, 10
1, 2, 3, 5, 9
1, 2, 3, 6, 8
1, 2, 4, 5, 8
1, 2, 4, 6, 7
1, 3, 4, 5, 7
2, 3, 4, 5, 6
Hence 7 solutions are there.
